item.description: The camera moves rightward and pans slightly leftward from a low angle, looking up at the exterior facade of a completed two-storey building constructed with unpainted reddish-tan bricks laid in an alternating long-face and short-face pattern with recessed mortar joints. From 0.0s to 4.0s, the right and central sections are prominent, showing upper-floor sliding glass windows with white frames, corbelled red-painted brick window hoods (chajjas), a rooftop parapet with open semi-circular brick arches, and lower-floor wooden-shuttered openings. Around 3.0s to 5.0s, a curved brick entrance arch with a blue sign reading 'TAKSHASHILA' enters at the lower left, along with an upper-floor semi-circular arch and a circular brick opening on the left wing. From 5.0s to 17.77s, the camera continues tracking right while framing the central gable—which features a curved parapet and a decorative perforated brick jali screen—alongside the arched and circular openings of the left wing. Green tree branches hang in the upper foreground, passing across the upper-right frame especially between 11.0s and 17.77s. At approximately 10.0s, a brief focus softness occurs before the image sharpens again by 11.0s.
